column3: The Hebrew repeats “Ammonites” here; NASB reads “Meunites,” as the Greek does.
“People came” is rendered “some came,” and “there they are” as “behold, they are”; NASB uses parentheses for “that is Engedi.”
“Gave his face” is rendered “turned his attention.”
NASB supplies “help.”
“Courtyard” is rendered “court.”
NASB repeats “are You not”; “there is not with you to hold ground” is rendered “no one can stand against You.”
“Dispossess” is rendered “drive out,” and “offspring” as “descendants.”
Close to the Hebrew.
NASB adds “or” and parentheses; “save” is rendered “deliver us.”
“Go in them” is rendered “invade”; NASB uses parentheses.
“Repaying” is rendered “rewarding,” and “caused us to possess” as “given us as an inheritance.” NASB adds “how.”
“Enter into judgment on them” is rendered “judge them,” and “there is not in us strength” as “we are powerless.”
“Little ones” is rendered “infants.”
“It was on him” is rendered “came upon”; NASB moves “in the midst of the assembly” forward.
“Pay attention” is rendered “Listen.”
“Wadi” is rendered “valley,” and “there” as “Behold.”
“Take your stand” is rendered “station yourselves,” and “victory” as “salvation”; “with you” is rendered “on your behalf.” “Before them” is rendered “to face them,” and NASB supplies “for.”
“Bowed low” is rendered “bowed his head.”
“A great voice upward” is rendered “a very loud voice.”
“Trust” is rendered “put your trust.”
“Adornment of holiness” is rendered “holy attire,” and “the equipped man” as “the army.” NASB supplies “Him.”
“A shout of joy” is rendered “singing,” and “ambushers” as “ambushes.” “Were defeated” is rendered “were routed.”
“Helped each on his neighbor to destruction” is rendered “helped to destroy one another.”
“Watchtower” is rendered “lookout,” and “turned to” as “looked toward.” “There was not an escaped remnant” is rendered “no one had escaped.”
The Hebrew reads “corpses”; NASB reads “garments,” as some manuscripts do. “To there was not carrying” is rendered “more than they could carry.”
NASB spells “Beracah.”
“From their enemies” is rendered “over their enemies.”
The two stringed instruments are reversed.
